boundaries.actual_step_quote: Composition of the two affine maps shows that commutativity is exactly $a_i(e^{v_i}-1)=b_i(e^{u_i}-1)$. Let $E(t)=(e^t-1)/t$ for $t\ne0$ and $E(0)=1$; its convergent series is $\sum_{n\ge0}t^n/(n+1)!$, so it is holomorphic and nonzero near zero. Since $a_i(o)\ne0$, the holomorphic function $\tau_i=(b_i/a_i)E(u_i)/E(v_i)$ is defined near $o$. The commutativity equation becomes exactly $v_i=\tau_i u_i$, and $\tau_i(o)=b_i(o)/a_i(o)$. The finitely many nonreal values permit one common neighborhood on which all $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i$ are nonzero. Thus all $\tau_i$ are nonzero, proving the equivalence of their zero logarithms and the asserted quotient limit. The argument is an identity of holomorphic functions on $Z$, so singular points cause no difficulty. [given, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: The compact case has no cusp tails and is explicitly allowed.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: Put $G=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$, $K=\mathrm{PSU}(2)$ and $V=\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$. Choose $X_1=\tfrac12\left(\begin{smallmatrix}i&0\\0&-i\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, $X_2=\tfrac12\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $X_3=\tfrac12\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&i\\i&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ in $\mathfrak k$, and put $Y_j=iX_j$. These $Y_j$ are an orthonormal tangent basis for curvature $-1$ hyperbolic space; for example $\exp(tY_1)$ moves the basepoint distance $|t|$, and the $K$ action rotates this basis. The matrix commutators give $[X_i,X_j]=\epsilon_{ijk}X_k$ and $[Y_i,Y_j]=i\epsilon_{ijk}Y_k$. On $V$ let $R_j=\operatorname{ad}Y_j$. Each $Y_j$ is Hermitian, so $R_j$ is self-adjoint for $\langle A,B\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(AB^*)$, by cyclicity of trace. The $K$ action is unitary for this product. [given, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: The zero closed form has the unique minimal-norm zero primitive.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: Represent $E$-valued forms by horizontal $K$-equivariant $V$-valued forms on $Q=\Gamma\backslash G$, expressing their coefficients in the left Maurer–Cartan frame. Indeed a frame $g$ identifies the fiber over $gK$ with $V$ by $\operatorname{Ad}g$, and replacing $g$ by $gk$ changes these coefficients by $\operatorname{Ad}k^{-1}$ and rotates the tangent indices. In these coefficients write $\varepsilon_j$ for exterior multiplication by the dual of $Y_j$ and $\iota_j$ for contraction by $Y_j$. The ordinary covariant differential of the $K$ connection is $D=\sum_j\varepsilon_jY_j$, because the horizontal part of $[Y_i,Y_j]$ is zero. Differentiating the fiber change $\operatorname{Ad}g$ gives $d_E=D+T$, where $T=\sum_j\varepsilon_jR_j$. These are actual coefficient formulas on all degrees, not definitions of a different connection. [step 1.1, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: The estimate concerns adjoint one-forms, the degree required by the later deformation proof.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: The invariant volume on $Q$ is the product of hyperbolic volume and normalized compact-fiber volume. Integration in a local bundle chart and then a partition of unity shows that integration of a $K$-invariant coefficient norm on $Q$ equals its integration on $M$. The left invariant fields $Y_j$ have zero divergence for this volume: $G$ is unimodular, since $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}Z)=0$ for the displayed Lie algebra basis, hence for all $Z$, and $\det\operatorname{Ad}(\exp Z)=1$. Right translation therefore preserves its Haar volume. Integration by parts on compact supports now gives $D^*=-\sum_j\iota_jY_j$ and $T^*=\sum_j\iota_jR_j$. The relations $\varepsilon_i\iota_j+\iota_j\varepsilon_i=\delta_{ij}$ show that $DT^*+T^*D+TD^*+D^*T=0$: the two anticommutator sums are respectively $\sum_jR_jY_j$ and its negative, since coefficient differentiation commutes with the constant matrices $R_j$. Thus $d_E\delta_E+\delta_Ed_E=DD^*+D^*D+H$, where $H=TT^*+T^*T$. All statements are $K$-equivariant and descend from $Q$ to $M$. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Strict positivity of the finite-dimensional algebraic operator excludes nonzero kernel.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: On one-form coefficients $a=(a_1,a_2,a_3)\in V^3$, the exterior-contraction relations give $(Ha)_i=\sum_jR_j^2a_i+\sum_j[R_i,R_j]a_j$. This finite-dimensional self-adjoint operator is positive definite. If $Ha=0$, positivity of $TT^*+T^*T$ gives $Ta=0$, namely $R_ia_j=R_ja_i$ for all $i,j$. Since $[R_i,R_j]=i\epsilon_{ijk}R_k$, the commutator sum in the displayed formula is a multiple of $R_ka_j-R_ja_k$ and vanishes. Consequently $0=\langle Ha,a\rangle=\sum_{i,j}\|R_ja_i\|^2$. Each $a_i$ commutes with all $Y_j$, which span $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$ over $\mathbb C$. A matrix commuting with all traceless matrices is scalar, and a traceless scalar is zero. Thus $a=0$. Compactness of the unit sphere in $V^3$ supplies $c>0$ with $H\ge cI$. [step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Cutoffs and graph-density arguments control the noncompact-domain integration by parts.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: For a compactly supported smooth one-form, integration by parts in step 3.1 and step 4.1 give $\|d_E\alpha\|_2^2+\|\delta_E\alpha\|_2^2=\|D\alpha\|_2^2+\|D^*\alpha\|_2^2+(H\alpha,\alpha)\ge c\|\alpha\|_2^2$. We next extend this inequality to the joint weak graph domain. On each cusp choose a smooth cutoff equal to one for $t\le R$, zero for $t\ge2R$, with derivative bounded by $C/R$, and set it equal to one on the compact core. These cutoffs $\chi_R$ have compact support and $|d\chi_R|\le C/R$. For a weak graph-domain form $v$, the product formulas $d_E(\chi_Rv)=\chi_Rd_Ev+d\chi_R\wedge v$ and $\delta_E(\chi_Rv)=\chi_R\delta_Ev-\iota_{\nabla\chi_R}v$ show convergence to $v$ in the joint graph norm. The same conclusion holds separately for each differential and codifferential and for forms of every degree. In the compact case take the cutoff identically one. [A1, step 3.1, step 4.1, given, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Cuspidal exhaustion has gradients tending to zero; no boundary term is discarded without a cutoff.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: Here are the local smoothing details needed to finish that graph-density argument. In a finite collection of trivializing charts around the support of $\chi_Rv$, every differential or codifferential is a first-order matrix operator $P=\sum_jA_j(x)\partial_j+B(x)$ with smooth coefficients. Multiplication by a subordinate smooth partition reduces to forms supported inside individual charts. For convolution with a smooth unit-mass kernel $\rho_\epsilon$, the difference $P(v*\rho_\epsilon)-(Pv)*\rho_\epsilon$ is a sum of integral operators with kernels $(A_j(x)-A_j(y))\partial_j\rho_\epsilon(x-y)+(\partial_jA_j)(y)\rho_\epsilon(x-y)$ and a zero-order coefficient commutator. The $L^1$ kernel bounds are uniform on the compact chart, by the mean-value bound for $A_j$ and scaling of $\rho_\epsilon$; thus these commutators are uniformly bounded on $L^2$. They tend to zero on smooth functions by differentiation of convolutions, hence on all $L^2$ functions by smooth approximation and the uniform bound. Therefore local mollification converges in each asserted graph norm, also for the direct sum operator $(d_E,\delta_E)$. The partition contributes only fixed zero-order commutators, so a finite sum completes the approximation by compactly supported smooth forms. Together with step 5.1 this proves the coercive inequality on the maximal joint graph domain. It also proves that maximal differentials are the adjoints of maximal formal codifferentials, since their compact-support integration-by-parts identities extend by this graph density. [A1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Closed L2 forms enter the Hilbert-space construction of a primitive.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: If $\alpha$ is smooth, the primitive $b$ is smooth. In a flat parallel frame on a coordinate ball, $d_Eb=\alpha$ is the ordinary componentwise distributional equation $db=\alpha$. A smooth closed one-form on a smaller star-shaped coordinate ball has a smooth primitive $b_0$, given by integrating along straight radial segments; differentiating the integral and using closedness verifies $db_0=\alpha$. Then $d(b-b_0)=0$ distributionally. Mollification on still smaller balls makes this difference a sequence of constants, so its distributional limit is constant as well. Thus $b=b_0+\text{constant}$ is smooth locally and hence globally. Its $L^2$ norm and the bound from step 8.1 remain unchanged. [step 8.1, algebra] ∎

boundaries.evidence: The theorem assumes k at least one, so the no-cusp case is outside its stated domain.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: The complete holonomy is irreducible and its adjoint invariants vanish. Indeed one cusp subgroup is a rank-two translation lattice fixing $\infty$. If all of $\Gamma$ fixed $\infty$, its elements would be similarities $z\mapsto az+b$. An element with $|a|\ne1$ would conjugate a fixed nonzero lattice translation to translations tending to the identity, contradicting discreteness. An element with $|a|=1$ and $a\ne1$ is elliptic about a vertical line, impossible in a torsion-free discrete group. Hence all elements would be translations, and the quotient would have infinite volume as height tends to zero. This contradicts the finite-volume hypothesis. Thus some element does not fix $\infty$. A traceless matrix invariant under the cusp group is a multiple of $E=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, by direct commutation with a nontrivial unipotent. A nonzero such matrix invariant under all of $\Gamma$ would force preservation of its kernel line, hence of $\infty$, a contradiction. Thus $H^0(M;E_{\operatorname{Ad}\rho_0})=0$. The same argument excludes a common invariant line for the holonomy matrices. The group centralizer in $G$ is trivial as well: a Möbius map commuting with the cusp translations fixes $\infty$ and is itself a translation, by its affine formula; a nonidentity such translation has unique fixed point $\infty$, so commuting with the entire group would force the whole group to fix $\infty$. [given, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: The complete parameter is u=0 and s_i=4; its peripheral eigenspace is unique.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: We specify the cohomology comparisons being used. The flat adjoint bundle has local parallel frames, obtained on simply connected balls by trivializing its defining covering construction. In such frames its differential is the componentwise ordinary exterior differential; integration of forms over simplices is compatible with the constant transition matrices and with Stokes. The usual local Poincaré contraction is explicit: integrate contraction by the radial vector along radial coordinate segments. A locally finite good cover by sufficiently small strongly convex metric balls therefore gives a Čech double complex whose form columns resolve the parallel local sections. Its positive Čech rows are contracted by $(hc)_{i_0\ldots i_{r-1}}=\sum_j\phi_jc_{ji_0\ldots i_{r-1}}$, for a subordinate partition of unity. The small-singular-cochain double complex has the same degree-zero columns, since every intersection is contractible; subdivision makes singular simplices subordinate to the cover, and the Čech rows contract by assigning a containing index to each small simplex. The two edge comparisons identify flat de Rham cohomology with singular cohomology with this local system, naturally for restrictions. These constructions also apply to compact support and to collars, so relative classes are represented by forms supported away from the ends. Finally $M$ is aspherical, with universal cover $\mathbb H^3$ contractible. Its lifted cellular or singular chains form a free resolution of $\mathbb C$ as a $\mathbb C\Gamma$-module; comparison of free resolutions by successive lifts gives the same cohomology as group cocycles. In degree one, this comparison is concretely integration of an equivariant closed form along a lifted group loop. These arguments establish the coefficient comparisons, rather than invoking an unproved twisted de Rham theorem. [A1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Specializing k=1 gives the full smooth ordinary curve and branched augmented curve.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: The representation scheme of a torus is smooth near its noncentral complete peripheral pair. Use local $SL_2$ lifts $A,B$ of the two generators, both near nontrivial commuting unipotents; their commutator is $I$ because its sign is locally constant and is positive at the basepoint. Choose a fixed vector $v$ with $v,Av$ independent at that point and hence nearby. For a commuting matrix $B$, write $Bv=av+bAv$; commutation then forces $B=aI+bA$ by applying both sides to the basis $v,Av$. This argument works over truncated power-series rings too, because the basis determinant is a unit. Put $C=A-(\operatorname{tr}A)I/2$ and write $B=\alpha I+\beta C$. Its determinant condition is $\alpha^2-\beta^2((\operatorname{tr}A)^2/4-1)=1$. At the complete pair $\alpha=1$, so [F3] solves uniquely for $\alpha$ in terms of $A$ and $\beta$. Thus the commuting-pair scheme is locally a smooth four-dimensional space, parametrized by the three coordinates of $A$ and one of $\beta$. In particular every representation over $\mathbb C[t]/(t^{n+1})$ near this pair extends one order further. [F3, given, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Noncentral parabolic pairs and irreducibility exclude extra centralizer or quotient degeneracy.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: Write $E_0=E_{\operatorname{Ad}\rho_0}$. The restriction $r_1:H^1(N;E_0)\to H^1(\partial N;E_0)$ is injective. If a closed smooth form represents a class in its kernel, on each cusp tail it equals $d_{E_0}b_i$ for a smooth section, by step 1.2. Subtract $d_{E_0}(\chi_i b_i)$ using a cutoff equal to one sufficiently far along that end and zero near the core. The resulting cohomologous closed form is compactly supported, hence square integrable, and is exact by [F1]. Thus the original class is zero. Equivalently the map $H^1(N,\partial N;E_0)\to H^1(N;E_0)$ vanishes. By [F2], its transpose, up to the harmless cap-boundary sign, is the map $H^2(N,\partial N;E_0)\to H^2(N;E_0)$, so that map also vanishes. The pair sequence therefore gives $r_2:H^2(N;E_0)\to H^2(\partial N;E_0)$ injective. It is onto because its cokernel embeds in $H^3(N,\partial N;E_0)$, which is dual to $H^0(N;E_0)=0$ by step 1.1. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Peripheral restriction detects H2 obstructions and supplies the exact deformation rank.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: We give the full obstruction construction. Suppose $\rho^{(n)}$ is a representation over $\mathbb C[t]/(t^{n+1})$ with constant term $\rho_0$. Choose arbitrary one-order lifts $\widetilde\rho(\gamma)$ of its values. The defect is uniquely $\widetilde\rho(\gamma)\widetilde\rho(\delta)\widetilde\rho(\gamma\delta)^{-1}=I+t^{n+1}c(\gamma,\delta)$ modulo $t^{n+2}$, with $c$ in the adjoint Lie algebra; this expression is read in the identity chart of $G$. Associativity gives $c(\gamma,\delta)+c(\gamma\delta,\epsilon)=\operatorname{Ad}_{\rho_0(\gamma)}c(\delta,\epsilon)+c(\gamma,\delta\epsilon)$, exactly the group two-cocycle relation. Replacing the lift at $\gamma$ by $(I+t^{n+1}b(\gamma))\widetilde\rho(\gamma)$ changes $c$ by $b(\gamma)+\operatorname{Ad}_{\rho_0(\gamma)}b(\delta)-b(\gamma\delta)$. Hence a one-order extension exists if and only if the class $[c]\in H^2(\Gamma;\operatorname{Ad}\rho_0)$ vanishes. The formulas commute with restriction to every subgroup. [A1, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Standard cusp L2 representatives are checked with their true exponential density.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: At a cusp the adjoint invariants are $\mathbb CE$, of dimension one. Torus duality and the Euler characteristic of a finite cellular local system give $\dim H^0(T_i;E_0)=\dim H^2(T_i;E_0)=1$ and $\dim H^1(T_i;E_0)=2$. Indeed every cell contributes three coefficient dimensions, so the alternating chain dimension is $3\chi(T_i)=0$. The pair sequence and step 2.1 give a short exact sequence $0\to H^1(N;E_0)\to H^1(\partial N;E_0)\to H^2(N,\partial N;E_0)\to0$. The last group is dual to the first by [F2]. Consequently $\dim H^1(N;E_0)=k$, while $r_2$ identifies $H^2(N;E_0)$ with $\mathbb C^k$. All these spaces are finite dimensional by the finite CW model in [F2]. [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Every augmented representation determines its selected-line eigenlog coordinate.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: The local lift of $\rho(u)(\lambda_i)$ commutes with $A_i(u)$: the commutator sign is locally constant and positive at the complete point. It acts on $\ell_i(u)$ by a nonzero holomorphic eigenvalue near its complete value; choose its sign to make this value $1$, and define $v_i$ as twice its near-zero logarithm. Choose a holomorphic change of frame sending $\ell_i(u)$ to $\mathbb Ce_1$, by adjoining a fixed complementary vector and normalizing the determinant locally. The resulting peripheral Möbius maps fix $\infty$ and act on its finite complement as $z\mapsto e^{u_i}z+a_i(u)$ and $z\mapsto e^{v_i}z+b_i(u)$. At $u=0$, their translations satisfy $a_i(0)\ne0$ and $b_i(0)/a_i(0)=\tau_i^0$. Apply [F4] to get $v_i=\tau_i(u)u_i$ with $\tau_i$ holomorphic and $\tau_i(0)=\tau_i^0$. Positivity of the imaginary part persists on a sufficiently small common neighborhood. For one cusp the holomorphic Taylor expansion gives $v(u)=\tau^0u+O(u^2)$. All constructions used representation matrices and cusp models; none used an ideal triangulation, or a positivity assumption about tetrahedra. [F4, step 9.1, given, algebra] ∎

boundaries.evidence: k is at least one; the nonempty complete polydisc supplies a valid fixed-point domain.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: Shrink to a closed convex polydisc $B_\epsilon=\{\|u\|_\infty\le\epsilon\}$ inside the holomorphy domain. Its compactness and continuity of the derivatives give a common Lipschitz constant $L$ for all $\tau_i$ there, by integrating their derivatives along line segments. Put $A=\max_i|\operatorname{Im}\tau_i(0)|^{-1}$ and shrink $\epsilon$ so that $AL\epsilon\le1/4$ and every $\operatorname{Im}\tau_i(u)$ stays nonzero on $B_\epsilon$. For any nonzero real pair $(p,q)$, $p+q\tau_i(0)\ne0$ and $|q/(p+q\tau_i(0))|\le A$. Moreover $|p+q\tau_i(0)|\ge c\sqrt{p^2+q^2}$ for one common $c>0$: the real-linear maps $(p,q)\mapsto p+q\tau_i(0)$ are invertible, and their moduli have a positive minimum on the unit circle. [A1, given, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: Infinite coefficients set w_i=a_i=0 and give exactly u_i=0.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: For a parameter tuple with finite pairs outside a sufficiently large radius $R$, define $a_i=q_i/(p_i+q_i\tau_i(0))$ and the $w_i$ in the Statement. At an infinite coordinate put $a_i=w_i=0$. On $B_\epsilon$ define $T_i(u)=w_i/[1+a_i(\tau_i(u)-\tau_i(0))]$. boundaries.actual_step_quote: We first give an isometry-equivariant way of blending maps into $\mathbb H^3$. Use the Lorentz form $\langle X,X\rangle=X_1^2+X_2^2+X_3^2-X_4^2$ and embed upper half-space by $\Phi(Z,Y)=(\operatorname{Re}Z/Y,\operatorname{Im}Z/Y,(|Z|^2+Y^2-1)/(2Y),(|Z|^2+Y^2+1)/(2Y))$. Direct substitution gives $\langle\Phi,\Phi\rangle=-1$, positive last coordinate, and differentiation gives the upper half-space metric $(|dZ|^2+dY^2)/Y^2$. Its coordinate matrix in $(\operatorname{Re}Z,\operatorname{Im}Z,Y)$ is $Y^{-2}I_3$, so its volume coefficient is the positive square root of $Y^{-6}$, namely $Y^{-3}$. The action of $G=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb C)$ is linear on these Lorentz coordinates. Indeed the equivalent Hermitian-matrix coordinate is $Y^{-1}\left(\begin{smallmatrix}|Z|^2+Y^2&Z\\\overline Z&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$; it is positive definite with determinant one, and $X\mapsto AXA^*$, for $A\in SL_2(\mathbb C)$, is linear on the four real Hermitian coordinates, preserves determinant and positivity, and is unchanged by replacing $A$ by $-A$. For positive weights summing to one, a weighted sum $S$ of future unit timelike vectors is future timelike: writing each vector as $(x,t)$ gives $t>|x|$, and the triangle inequality gives this strict inequality for the sum. Thus $B(S)=S/\sqrt{-\langle S,S\rangle}$ is well defined and smooth. It commutes with every $G$ action. If every input equals $X$, its value is $X$. This is a normalized Lorentz sum, rather than an undefined linear average inside a manifold. [F3, given, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: The complete parameter reproduces the original developing map and metric.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: Fix an end and omit its index temporarily. Choose the frames in [F1] so that at zero its original developing map is $(x,y,t)\mapsto(a(0)(x+\tau(0)y),e^t)$ on $\mathbb R^2\times[0,\infty)$. The deck generators add one to $x$ and $y$. Such a normalization is obtained by a fixed translation and dilation of a lift of the original horoball; it only fixes the origin and the level called $t=0$. Write $\zeta=x+\tau(u)y$, $L=u\zeta$, $w=(1-e^u)/a(u)$ and $B=\sqrt{(1+|w|^2)/(1+e^{2t}|w|^2)}$, choosing the positive square root. Put $E(z)=(e^z-1)/z$ with $E(0)=1$. Define an end map $\Psi_u=(Z_u,Y_u)$ by $Y_u=e^t|e^L|B$ and $Z_u=a(u)\zeta E(L)/E(u)+e^L(e^{2t}-1)\overline w/((1+e^{2t}|w|^2)(1+B))$. All these formulas are smooth in $(x,y,t,\operatorname{Re}u,\operatorname{Im}u)$, and in the other deformation coordinates: $a,\tau$ are holomorphic, $a$ and $E(u)$ are nonzero after shrinking, and every real denominator is positive. At $u=0$ they give precisely $(a(u)(x+\tau(u)y),e^t)$, including when other deformation coordinates are nonzero. At the complete parameter they give the original developing map. Consequently their convergence, with every derivative, is uniform on each fixed compact coordinate collar. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: A primitive full turn is one angular period, which produces an ordinary smooth core.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: Choose product coordinates $T_i^2\times[0,\infty)$ on the ends, and include their collars through $t=2$ in a compact set $K$. The given complete developing map identifies the universal cover of $M$ with $\mathbb H^3$, with deck action $\rho_0$. Cover $K$ by finitely many simply connected evenly covered coordinate sets $U_j$ and choose one lift $\widetilde U_j$ for each. On an open neighborhood $V$ of $K$ covered by these sets, use [F2] to choose a subordinate smooth partition $\phi_j$. Pull each function to each component $\rho_0(\gamma)\widetilde U_j$ and extend it by zero; denote this lifted function by $\phi_{\gamma j}$. Its support stays inside that component. These functions are locally finite and sum to one on the inverse image of $V$. Put $D_{\gamma j}(x,u)=\rho_u(\gamma)\rho_0(\gamma)^{-1}x$ and let $D^{\mathrm{core}}_u(x)$ be the Lorentz blend of the points $D_{\gamma j}(x,u)$ with weights $\phi_{\gamma j}(x)$. The sums are locally finite and smooth. The deck identities for the weights and $D_{\delta\gamma,j}(\rho_0(\delta)x,u)=\rho_u(\delta)D_{\gamma j}(x,u)$ show exact $\rho_u$ equivariance. At zero every input is $x$, so $D^{\mathrm{core}}_0(x)=x$. [A1, F2, step 1.1, given, construct, algebra]

boundaries.evidence: The nonzero axial period prevents screw fixed points and cone singularities.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: When $u\ne0$, put $c=1/w=a/(1-e^u)$ and $C=|c|$. The identity $(1-B)/w=(e^{2t}-1)\overline w/((1+e^{2t}|w|^2)(1+B))$ rewrites the preceding formula as $Z_u=c(1-Be^L)$, $Y_u=e^t|e^L|B$. On adding one to $x$, these become $Z\mapsto e^uZ+a$, $Y\mapsto e^{\operatorname{Re}u}Y$. Commutativity gives $a(e^v-1)=b(e^u-1)$, so $c(1-e^v)=b$; adding one to $y$ gives the other peripheral isometry. When $u=0$, the translation formula in step 1.2 gives the same equivariance because $v=0$ and $b=a\tau$. Compose $\Psi_u$ with the inverse of the frame from [F1]; this gives a map $D^{\mathrm{end}}_u$ on a chosen lifted end, equivariant under its peripheral subgroup. Extend to all its deck translates by $D^{\mathrm{end}}_u(\rho_0(\gamma)x)=\rho_u(\gamma)D^{\mathrm{end}}_u(x)$. This is well defined because two descriptions differ by a peripheral deck transformation. [F1, step 1.2, algebra, construct]

boundaries.evidence: Metric coefficients agree on full collars and the smooth axis charts are explicit.
boundaries.actual_step_quote: On the compact quotient $K$, the last construction converges to the identity in every derivative as $u\to0$, in fixed local lift charts. To see uniformity without an assertion about infinitely many deck transformations, cover $K$ by finitely many smaller relatively compact chart pieces and lift each piece once. Only finitely many of the locally finite functions $\phi_{\gamma j}$ meet those compact lifts. Only these finitely many matrices $\rho_u(\gamma)\rho_0(\gamma)^{-1}$ enter the derivative estimates there, and each converges smoothly to the identity. Invertibility of a matrix is open; compactness and [F2] therefore give one neighborhood of zero on which $D^{\mathrm{core}}_u$ is a local diffeomorphism at all points over $K$. Its pullback metric descends by equivariance, is hyperbolic, and converges smoothly to the original metric on $K$. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

boundaries.actual_step_quote: The end map is a local diffeomorphism on its entire domain. For $u=0$ this follows directly from the translation formula and $\operatorname{Im}\tau>0$. Direct differentiation using [F3] gives $dr^2+\sinh^2r\,d\theta^2+\cosh^2r\,ds^2$. The map in step 2.2 is precisely $r(t)=\operatorname{arsinh}(Ce^{-t})$, $s=\log\sqrt{C^2+1}+\operatorname{Re}L$, $\theta=\arg(-c)+\operatorname{Im}L$. The choice of the constant argument is immaterial modulo $2\pi$. The real linear map $(x,y)\mapsto(\operatorname{Re}L,\operatorname{Im}L)$ has determinant $\operatorname{Im}(\overline u v)=|u|^2\operatorname{Im}\tau>0$, and $r'(t)\ne0$. Thus the differential is invertible everywhere for finite $t$. For $t\ge T$ its image is the whole punctured tube $0<r\le R(T)$, where $R(T)=\operatorname{arsinh}(Ce^{-T})$, and $(s,\theta)$ before angular reduction range over all $\mathbb R^2$. No discreteness of the full peripheral image is required for this local assertion. [F2, F3, step 1.2, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

boundaries.actual_step_quote: Finally the same formulas give convergence of volume, including for varying simultaneous slope tuples. All assertions of the Statement follow. [F2, F3, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 5.2, step 8.1, algebra] ∎
